reply_text:
I found four dated AI predictions Musk made in 2017. Three of them are about Tesla's self-driving cars, so you may decide those fall outside "about AI".

- **AI beating humans at everything (June 2017 tweet).** This is the clearest AI forecast. Musk replied to a New Scientist headline that said AI would beat humans at everything by 2060. He wrote: "Probably closer to 2030 to 2040 imo." I only saw the tweet's text embedded in a Futurism article. I did not open the tweet itself.
- **Self-driving forecasts (TED, April 2017; governors' meeting, July 15, 2017).** He said a Tesla would drive itself from Los Angeles to New York by the end of 2017. He said a self-driving car you could sleep in was "about two years" away. He also said almost all cars produced would be self-driving within 10 years. I read these in transcripts on singjupost.com, which is not TED's or the governors' official site. TED's own transcript page opened but had no transcript text. The two-year answer was to a question that set legal rules aside and asked only about the technology.

Other points:
- **Pages that didn't open.** The CNBC year-end roundup of Musk's 2017 AI comments would not open, so I quote nothing from it.
- **Left out.** His warnings that AI is an existential risk and his line that robots will "do everything better than us" give no date. His "five to 10 percent chance" of making AI safe (Rolling Stone, November 2017) was seen only in search snippets and also has no date. His Dubai talk at the World Government Summit (February 2017) and his Neuralink timelines were not opened.
- **Budget.** I ran 7 of the 12 searches and used all 6 page openings.
